decision_conditions: The proposed development, by virtue of its size, siting, form and design, would result in a  disproportionate and unsympathetic addition to the property which would fail to appropriately integrate with the dwelling or the immediate surrounding built form of the Conservation Area. The first floor extension would fail to appear as appropriately subservient which, together with the unsatisfactory design, would result in the extension appearing as a disagreeing and discordant addition, and would introduce an uncharacteristic feature to the Close, diluting the existing uniform character exhibited. Furthermore, the immediate proximity of the extension to the side boundary at first floor level would also result in a visually cramped appearance, over and above what currently exists at the site, to the detriment of the visual amenities of the area. Overall, the proposal would fail to create a positive satisfactory appearance and design which improves and enhances the character and appearance of

The proposed first floor rear opening, by virtue of its siting, height, openable nature and the limited separation distances involved, would result in the introduction of a harmful level of overlooking to the rear of the site, significantly impacting upon the privacy of an adjacent neighbour, namely no. 40 Halford Road. As such, the proposal would represent an un-neighbourly form of development which would not achieve a satisfactory relationship with adjacent dwellings, failing to preserve the amenity of a neighbouring property. The proposed development would therefore not conform to the requirements of Policies DMHB 11 and DMHD1 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020).
description: Erection of first floor extension and associated alterations to allow for part-conversion of roof space to habitable use
